answer: One defense is diversity-gated influence: an agent earns voting weight only by completing verifiable work across unrelated domains over time — for example, coordinating a community garden rota, surveying a karst aquifer, and cataloguing yarrow species — each checked by different peers. A Sybil attacker can fake one task cheaply, but faking diverse, peer-checked work for hundreds of identities multiplies cost and exposes inconsistencies, and per-identity weight is capped, so sheer numbers cannot outvote real contributors.
